summary: A 1953 federal survey note places a fire tower 75 ft from a 1918 survey station near Conley; no source says what remains today.

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey monumented the survey station stamped CONLEY 1918. This is the survey station, not the tower.
A fire tower had been built about 75 ft (23 m) southwest of the station by the 1953 recovery note. The note gives no build date or builder.
Last recovery note in the datasheet; it says only that the station was recovered as described.

notes_for_editor: Only evidence for the tower is the 1953 NGS recovery note; no source gives its builder, build date, design, staffing, use or fate, and no source describes the site today. Elevation disagreement left open: the tnlandforms list gives 1,035 with no unit (its elevation heading names no unit), so the story reads it as feet, which makes it 7 ft below the survey station's NAVD 88 height of 1,042.0 ft (317.61 m); no source explains the difference. County: list and datasheet say DeKalb; the Wikipedia Conley infobox map shows the community in Clayton County. Story follows DeKalb. The 1953 directions to the station and tower were left out: they are old and may not reflect current access or ownership. Do not publish them as access.
